title: Settings preview reports no write while authority loading rewrites active artifacts
observed_behavior: preview_settings_patch documents a no-write PSD1 preview and returns writes_config=false, but first calls the production authority loader. When the JSON store exists, that loader unconditionally executes the full store/PSD1/projection promotion, verification, backup, and snapshot path. A disposable production-like probe observed one save_config_document call and creation of both store and projection while the successful response still reported writes_config=false.
expected_invariant: A route documented and reported as preview-only must not mutate the JSON authority, active PSD1, projection manifest, backups, or snapshots. Required authority verification must use a pure read path, and any explicit repair or regeneration must be truthfully identified and mutation-gated.
root_cause: Authority read/validation and authority repair/projection are combined in load_settings_authority_for_service, while preview treats that mutating loader as a read operation and hard-codes no-write evidence.
failure_scenario: An operator previews a harmless settings patch after the active PSD1 was manually edited, made read-only, or drifted from the JSON authority. The preview silently overwrites the PSD1 from JSON, creates/updates evidence artifacts and backups, or fails due to write permissions even though no save was confirmed and the response claims no write.
evidence: settings_patch_facade.py lines 58-65 states the no-write contract and calls service.load_settings_authority before candidate construction
settings_store.py lines 594-603 unconditionally calls _promote_envelope_and_projection for an existing store
settings_store.py lines 521-548 writes and verifies the store, PSD1, projection manifest, and last-good snapshots
settings_patch_policy.py line 429 always reports writes_config=false
disposable isolated probe returned {ok:true, projection_created:true, reported_writes_config:false, save_config_document_calls_during_preview:1, store_exists:true}
affected_flows: Settings save helper that obtains a fresh backend preview before confirmation
JSON authority drift detection and PSD1 regeneration
read-only operator review and automation callers
existing_safeguards: The promotion is held under the OS authority lock; Store and projection use atomic same-directory replacement; PSD1 is schema-validated and PowerShell round-trip checked; Promotion verifies hashes and attempts rollback on failure
safeguard_gap: Atomicity makes the hidden mutation safer but does not make it authorized or accurately reported. The preview contract has no way to distinguish pure authority verification from a repair/regeneration write.
tests_present: tests/python/desktop/test_application_facade_settings_patch.py covers preview results through a dummy service that does not expose the production authority-load side effect
tests/python/desktop/test_settings_store.py covers existing-store projection regeneration but not through the preview contract
tests_missing: Production-like preview test asserting byte-for-byte stability of store, PSD1, projection, backups, and snapshots
Read-only filesystem preview test proving no write permission is required
Explicit repair/regeneration command test if drift repair remains an intended operator mutation
Response-evidence test binding writes_config to actual filesystem calls
recommended_remediation: Split settings authority access into a pure locked read/validate operation and an explicit repair/projection operation. Use the pure operation for preview and review-confirmation construction. If repair is necessary before preview, return a blocked response with actionable repair guidance or run a separately named, strictly confirmed repair command; derive writes_config evidence from the executed path.
remediation_risk: Medium-high: load_settings_authority is shared by startup, workspace, preview, and save flows. Separating read from repair must preserve JSON-authority precedence, last-good recovery, lock coverage, and startup regeneration without introducing stale candidates.
validation_rung: Targeted settings facade/store tests with isolated real filesystem artifacts, strict confirmation and drift/recovery tests, Local API settings preview smoke, packaged WebView preview behavior, and strict change-packet coverage; no real media required.
prior_audit_relationship: New root cause discovered during current line review. Prior audits described explicit PSD1 import preview as no-write and JSON-authority regeneration as safe, but did not reconcile that production patch preview invokes the mutating authority loader.

title: Idempotent settings replay bypasses complete review confirmation and still rewrites authority
observed_behavior: The save flow evaluates and executes its idempotent-replay branch before calling the complete review-confirmation validator. A partial confirmation containing only authority_config_digest, candidate_config_digest, and request_digest can satisfy replay predicates without schema_version, preview_id, base_config_digest, review_entries_digest, or changed/removed key binding. The branch calls save_settings_authority even though the current authority already equals the candidate. A normalized disposable probe returned ok=true and idempotent_replay=true with one authority-save call from such a partial confirmation and no changed keys.
expected_invariant: Every settings mutation, including an idempotent retry that touches disk, must require the complete backend-issued review confirmation. Once an already-durable candidate is proven, replay should return prior/current durable evidence without performing another promotion.
root_cause: Replay classification is ordered before strict review-confirmation validation, and replay is implemented by re-invoking the authoritative saver instead of as a read-only durable-state result.
failure_scenario: A caller constructs a partial confirmation from observable digests and repeatedly submits a no-op patch with confirm_save=true. Each request bypasses the full preview binding, rewrites store/PSD1/projection/snapshots, and can consume backups, contend on locks, fail mid-transaction, or create misleading mutation evidence despite no configuration change.
evidence: settings_patch_facade.py lines 267-290 computes replay from only three digest fields and calls authority_saver
settings_patch_facade.py lines 291-295 performs no-change handling and full review validation only after the replay branch
settings_patch_policy.py lines 175-200 requires seven digest/identity fields plus exact changed/removed lists in the normal path
settings_store.py lines 731-759 still invokes the full promotion for a durable candidate equality retry
isolated normalized probe accepted a forged partial confirmation and recorded one authority saver call
affected_flows: JSON store and PSD1 projection durability evidence
existing_safeguards: confirm_save must be the literal boolean true; Replay requires current authority digest to equal the submitted candidate and reconstructed merged digest; OS lock and store CAS prevent a different configuration from being silently written; Promotion remains validated, atomic for normal writes, and rollback guarded
safeguard_gap: The digest predicates constrain replay to the already-current configuration, but do not prove that the operator reviewed the exact preview or justify another disk mutation. Missing review fields are never checked on this branch.
tests_present: tests/python/desktop/test_application_facade_settings_patch.py covers a legitimate durable replay and expects two authority-save calls
tests/python/desktop/test_settings_store_concurrency.py covers durable retry at the store CAS layer
tests_missing: Replay test rejecting confirmations missing any full review field
Replay test rejecting tampered preview_id, base digest, review-entry digest, or changed/removed lists
Read-only idempotent replay test asserting zero saver calls and byte-stable authority/projection artifacts
Repeated replay and crash/error evidence test
recommended_remediation: Run settings_save_review_confirmation_error before replay classification. After complete binding succeeds, classify already-durable equality under the current locked authority read and return idempotent replay evidence without calling save_settings_authority. If an explicit repair write is needed, expose it separately and make its mutation/confirmation contract explicit.
remediation_risk: Medium: replay behavior is part of lost-response recovery. Reordering must preserve legitimate retry success, authority conflict semantics, lock coverage, reload verification, and compatibility with callers that retain a complete backend preview confirmation.
validation_rung: Targeted settings patch policy/facade/store tests, lost-response and repeated-replay tests with real temporary authority files, strict JSON/confirmation Local API smoke, and strict change-packet coverage; no real media required.
prior_audit_relationship: New root cause. The prior lost-update finding led to cross-process CAS and durable-retry support, but current replay ordering introduced a narrower strict-confirmation and no-op-write gap distinct from the repaired concurrency race.

title: Settings-store test double breaks on Windows and overstates rollback coverage
observed_behavior: The direct settings-store module errors in three of seven tests on Windows because its dummy saver uses Path.write_text without newline='', converting serializer LF bytes to CRLF before the production hash verifier. A focused retry reproduced SettingsStoreError at settings_store.py line 546; a byte probe observed five LF-to-CRLF conversions and unequal hashes. Production atomic_write_text fixes newlines and is unaffected. The rollback test sets fail_save, which raises before the PSD1 write, so it never reaches the projection-manifest write named by the test. The import test name claims apply-confirmation coverage but only executes preview.
expected_invariant: The Windows-first settings-store regression suite must execute production-faithful byte semantics, pass for valid authority operations, and inject failures at the exact named transaction boundary. Test names and assertions must truthfully describe the paths exercised.
root_cause: The hand-written service test double reimplements production persistence with platform-default newline translation and a coarse pre-write failure switch, instead of delegating to the atomic saver or providing boundary-specific fault injection.
failure_scenario: A real store migration, drift regeneration, last-good recovery, projection rollback, or import-confirmation regression lands. The high-risk direct suite is already red on Windows for fixture-only reasons, and its nominal projection-failure case stops before projection writing, so maintainers either ignore the suite or falsely infer recovery coverage that was never exercised.
evidence: test_settings_store.py lines 72-78 raises before save or writes with Path.write_text platform newline behavior
three tests failed with Settings PSD1 projection verification failed after atomic replacement; focused retry failed identically
byte-level probe produced five CRLF sequences in the dummy output and different expected/actual SHA-256 values
file_io.py lines 68-89 opens the production temporary file with newline='' and atomically replaces the target
separate late projection-manifest failure probe restored store, PSD1, and projection bytes, proving the normal source rollback path while exposing the checked-in test's vacuity
test_settings_store.py lines 319-343 calls import preview only and makes no apply/confirmation assertion
affected_flows: Settings JSON authority migration and projection regeneration regression evidence
Three-artifact rollback and cleanup regression evidence
existing_safeguards: Production file_io uses fixed newline bytes, fsync, same-directory atomic replacement, retries, and temp cleanup; Production promotion verifies committed store, manifest, and PSD1 hash; A dedicated concurrency suite passed all 11 lock/CAS/crash/retry cases; Disposable late-failure probe confirmed normal rollback of all three artifacts
safeguard_gap: Production safeguards do not repair a non-faithful test double. The broken module cannot supply clean release evidence, and its failure injection does not reach the recovery boundary it claims to test.
tests_present: tests/python/desktop/test_settings_store.py contains seven direct store tests but three currently error on Windows
tests/python/desktop/test_settings_store_concurrency.py passes 11 independent multiprocessing and failure-path tests
tests/python/desktop/test_application_facade_settings_patch.py passes strict patch and import confirmation tests at facade level
tests_missing: Production-faithful saver fixture using atomic_write_text or ConfigSaveRunner byte semantics
Fault injection at projection manifest atomic replacement after store and PSD1 writes
Assertions for all three original byte sequences, backup behavior, and temporary-file cleanup after late failure
Actual import apply calls covering missing, false, non-boolean, and true confirm_import
Cross-platform run proving byte-stable serializer/save/hash behavior
recommended_remediation: Replace the dummy's persistence implementation with the production atomic write helper or ConfigSaveRunner-compatible behavior. Inject projection failure by patching the projection manifest atomic_write_text call after successful store and PSD1 writes; assert restoration of exact bytes and no temporary residue. Split or rename the import preview test and add real apply-confirmation cases.
remediation_risk: Low-medium: test-only changes, but fault injection must target the intended call deterministically without mocking away production lock, CAS, serialization, verification, or rollback behavior.
validation_rung: Run the direct settings-store and concurrency modules on Windows plus a case-sensitive platform, the settings facade/policy suites, generated summary checks if tests change, and strict change-packet coverage; no real media required.
prior_audit_relationship: New test-evidence defect discovered while revalidating the prior settings authority findings. The July 9 audit did not execute tests, and the July 19 evidence did not report this current Windows fixture failure or the vacuous projection-failure injection.

title: JavaScript summary fabricates an import graph from quoted runtime text
observed_behavior: The current generated summary lists fragments such as exported && byId( and several window globals as in-repo imports even though presetLibrary.js contains no ES-module import, export, or dynamic import declaration. The official freshness check passes and exact render_summary reproduction produces the same malformed list.
expected_invariant: Generated summaries must describe actual dependency edges in the source they fingerprint; a current and reproducible summary must not fabricate imports from strings or ordinary runtime expressions.
root_cause: The JavaScript import extractor scans regex-shaped text without lexical awareness and treats export-like tokens inside quoted strings and ordinary expressions as module specifiers.
failure_scenario: An agent or generated dependency map treats presetLibrary.js as importing nonexistent modules, opens irrelevant files, infers false ownership edges, or misses a real architecture violation hidden by noisy fabricated dependencies.
evidence: Summary lines 18-20 contain syntactically impossible import fragments and window globals.
A bounded source search returned NO_ES_MODULE_IMPORT_OR_EXPORT_DECLARATIONS.
refresh_summaries --check passed for all 120 assigned source/summary pairs.
Direct render_summary reproduction matched all 120 assigned summaries byte-for-byte, proving this is deterministic extractor output rather than stale hand editing.
existing_safeguards: Source SHA-256 and generator fingerprint bind the summary to current inputs.
Freshness and reproducibility checks detect stale or hand-edited summaries.
safeguard_gap: Those checks prove deterministic freshness, not semantic correctness; no JavaScript fixture asserts that quoted export text and ordinary function calls cannot become import edges.
tests_present: Official refresh_summaries freshness check and direct render_summary reproduction.
tests_missing: JavaScript extractor fixture with export/import-like words inside strings and template literals.
Negative assertion that non-module scripts expose an empty in-repo import list.
recommended_remediation: Make JavaScript dependency extraction lexical or AST-aware, or at minimum strip comments and literals and require import/export grammar at statement boundaries. Regenerate affected summaries and add negative fixtures for this exact source pattern.
remediation_risk: low to medium: changing extraction can alter many generated dependency summaries, so compare the complete before/after edge set and retain dynamic-import coverage
validation_rung: Focused context-extractor tests, full generated-summary regeneration/check, orphan/freshness check, and dependency-map diff review. Real media is not required.
prior_audit_relationship: New current-hash generated-context defect; no current worker finding referenced presetLibrary.js summary imports.

title: The setup wizard's CPU default generates a VideoPreset rejected by the canonical contract

locations.symbol: CPU video profile and manual preset selection

observed_behavior: Config setup chooses libx265 with VideoPreset=medium as the default when no supported GPU is detected, and its local compatibility helper accepts that pair. The canonical schema, engine choice registry, Python option policy, and Config model allow only p1 through p7 for VideoPreset. A direct probe returned libx265_medium=true from the setup helper while Config rejected medium.
expected_invariant: Every setup-generated config must satisfy the same persisted-key contract consumed by the desktop backend and media engine. CPU encoder speed belongs in CpuEncodePreset; selecting CPU must not repurpose VideoPreset with an incompatible enum.
root_cause: The setup slice applies libx265 FFmpeg speed-preset names to the global VideoPreset key, while the active architecture separates descriptor VideoPreset p1-p7 from CpuEncodePreset names such as medium.
failure_scenario: On a host without a detected supported GPU, the recommended/default setup path selects the CPU row, writes VideoPreset=medium, then produces a config the canonical backend and generated schema reject. First-run deployment cannot complete coherently without the operator understanding an internal key split.
evidence: ConfigFile.ps1 line 183 defines the CPU row as libx265/medium and lines 205-206 persist both values.
Manual CPU tuning at lines 214-225 again writes ultrafast through veryslow into VideoPreset.
Test-VideoPresetCompatibility returned true for libx265/medium and false for libx265/p5.
Config(VideoCodec='libx265', VideoPreset='medium') raised the canonical p1-p7 validation error.
The generated JSON schema and engine choice registry both enumerate only p1-p7.
existing_safeguards: The setup tool has a codec-specific compatibility helper.
Canonical Python/schema validation rejects the invalid persisted value before normal backend use.
CpuEncodePreset exists with the intended libx265 speed-preset enum.
safeguard_gap: The setup helper duplicates and contradicts the canonical contract, so its own successful choice is not deployable and the safest no-GPU default is the broken branch.
tests_present: Canonical config and option-policy tests cover the p1-p7 VideoPreset contract.
tests_missing: End-to-end setup test that selects the no-GPU CPU default and validates the emitted config with the canonical schema/backend.
Parity test binding setup choices to choice_registry and Config.
recommended_remediation: Keep VideoPreset on a canonical p1-p7 value for every profile, and set CpuEncodePreset=medium when CPU fallback or libx265 policy is selected. Derive setup choices from the canonical registry and add a CPU-only emitted-config regression.
remediation_risk: medium: setup key mapping changes must preserve existing CPU quality, descriptor routing, and GPU fallback behavior without altering FFmpeg command policy
validation_rung: Focused setup emission and PowerShell compatibility tests, canonical Config/schema/option-policy validation, packaged first-run setup on a no-GPU fixture, and strict change-packet coverage. Real media is not required unless encoder routing or command generation is changed.
prior_audit_relationship: New current-hash setup/contract drift; no current finding covered the libx265 medium value in ConfigFile.ps1.

title: Incomplete encoder capability evidence is still labeled Ready
observed_behavior: The capability adapter calculates state and operator_status before validating the five required v2 evidence sections. A syntactically valid report with one available active CPU encoder and no evidence returns operator_status=Ready and operator_status_state=ready while its errors array says freshness, resolved_config, ffmpeg, host, and selected_descriptor_chain are all missing.
expected_invariant: Any missing required capability evidence must make the operator status fail closed to Review or Blocked; a payload must never simultaneously report Ready and contain capability-completeness errors.
root_cause: The state/status assignment occurs at lines 268-269, but required-evidence errors are appended at lines 273-277 and status is never recomputed before the response is returned.
failure_scenario: A truncated, partially migrated, or producer-bugged v2 capability report reaches Settings. The prominent readiness state says Ready even though provenance, freshness, host, FFmpeg, and descriptor selection proof are absent, encouraging an operator to trust unsupported encoder posture.
evidence: Current source computes state before required evidence validation.
A no-write direct call with schema mediapipeline.encoder_capabilities.v2 and an active available libx265 row returned Ready/ready plus the exact five-field incomplete-evidence error.
The response preserves that contradiction in operator_status, operator_status_state, summary_lines, and errors.
existing_safeguards: Schema, row availability, activation readiness, and hardware runtime proof can add errors before the initial state calculation.
The errors and summary arrays retain the missing-evidence message.
safeguard_gap: Consumers that prioritize the normalized status field over detail text receive a false positive, and no final consistency assertion binds Ready to an empty errors list.
tests_present: Encoder capability and preset policy tests cover several available/unavailable descriptor facts.
tests_missing: Required v2 evidence field omission matrix.
Invariant test that Ready implies errors is empty and all required evidence sections are populated.
recommended_remediation: Validate and normalize all required evidence before computing state/status, or recompute status after every error source. Add a response invariant that any error forces at least Review.
remediation_risk: low: this changes evidence classification only, but frontend status ordering and launch-readiness presentation should be checked for intended fail-closed behavior
validation_rung: Focused settings-policy capability tests, Local API workspace contract tests, WebView rendering smoke for incomplete evidence, and strict change-packet coverage. Real media is not required.
prior_audit_relationship: New current-hash evidence-ordering defect; exact symbol and incomplete-evidence searches found no prior finding.

title: PresetV2 apply silently ignores most audio, subtitle, verification, filter, and publish policy
observed_behavior: PresetV2 exposes routing, dimensions, filters, video, audio, subtitles, container, guards, verification, publish, and advanced sections, but its apply adapter emits only 26 routing/video/container/size keys plus ExtraVideoFlags. Preset library preview and confirmed apply pass exactly that partial patch to settings save without warning that the remaining sections are unsupported. A valid preset requesting AAC force-transcode, BDPGS conversion, and disabled duration matching produced no audio, BDPGS, or verification key in the patch.
expected_invariant: Applying a validated PresetV2 must either persist every representable policy field with equivalent semantics or reject/label unsupported sections before confirmation. A full-model apply action must not silently retain unrelated prior media policy.
root_cause: The legacy adapter was implemented as a display/migration subset, then reused as the authoritative preset-library apply patch without a field-coverage contract or unsupported-field check.
failure_scenario: An operator imports and applies a safety or compatibility preset that requires audio transcode, subtitle conversion/preservation, verification, filters, or publish behavior. The command succeeds and updates visible routing fields, but old settings remain active for the omitted sections, so subsequent media can be processed under a materially different policy than the reviewed preset.
evidence: PresetV2 declares eleven nested policy sections at preset_policy.py lines 351-361.
legacy_config_patch_from_preset_v2 maps only 26 keys and has no audio, subtitle, verification, publish, filter, or most advanced mappings.
Preset library apply preview and save use only legacy_patch.

A no-write reproduction showed audio forceTranscode=true/transcodeCodec=aac, convertBdpgsToSrt=true, and requireDurationMatch=false in the validated preset while audio_keys_in_patch, bdpgs_keys_in_patch, and verification_keys_in_patch were all empty.
existing_safeguards: PresetV2 validation rejects malformed section values.
Apply requires confirm_apply and the downstream settings save confirmation path.
Preview returns legacy_patch for a careful operator to inspect.
safeguard_gap: Neither validation nor preview reports that most validated policy is discarded, and confirmation binds only the reduced patch rather than the full preset semantics.
tests_present: Preset policy contract tests exercise selected legacy adapter mappings and invalid persisted-key handling.
Preset library tests cover basic save/list behavior.
tests_missing: Field-by-field PresetV2-to-config apply coverage matrix.
Negative apply test for any unsupported non-default field.
End-to-end preset apply proving audio, subtitle, verification, filters, guards, and publish settings match the reviewed preset.
recommended_remediation: Define an explicit complete PresetV2-to-stable-config mapping and assert coverage for every model field. Until complete, make apply fail closed when any unsupported field differs from the current/default value and show exact unsupported paths in preview.
remediation_risk: high: completing the mapping changes high-risk media policy across audio, subtitles, verification, and publish; preserve backend ownership and require representative real-media validation for any newly applied behavior
validation_rung: Exhaustive adapter round-trip and preset-library preview/save tests, settings schema/policy tests, Local API/WebView confirmation tests, then representative real-media audio/subtitle/verification/publish validation before enabling expanded mappings.
prior_audit_relationship: New current-hash preset-application defect; no current finding referenced legacy_config_patch_from_preset_v2 or preset library apply completeness.

title: A malformed preset-library records field is treated as empty and overwritten on save
observed_behavior: When presets.json is valid JSON with an object root but records is not a list, the loader silently substitutes an empty list. Save then appends only the new record and atomically replaces the original file. A disposable reproduction with a records object containing keep-me returned save_ok=true and rewrote the library to only new, with old_payload_preserved=false.
expected_invariant: Malformed or unsupported persisted state must fail closed without replacing the original bytes. Any intentional schema migration must preserve or backup all recoverable records and report the transformation.
root_cause: _load_library conflates an absent/invalid records type with a genuinely empty library and drops non-mapping list entries silently; the save path trusts that lossy normalized result as complete authority.
failure_scenario: A prior version, manual edit, partial migration, or producer defect stores records as an object or mixed collection. Listing looks empty, and the next ordinary preset save permanently replaces all prior content without warning or recovery evidence.
evidence: The loader explicitly assigns records=[] for every non-list value.
The save path immediately rebuilds and atomically replaces presets.json from library['records'].
A temporary-state reproduction preserved valid JSON throughout yet lost the existing keep-me payload after a successful save.
Exact current finding search found no prior preset_library.py finding.
existing_safeguards: Invalid JSON and non-object roots raise an error.
The replacement itself is fsynced and atomic.
Individual new presets are validated as PresetV2 before save.
safeguard_gap: Atomic replacement faithfully commits the lossy interpretation, and there is no schema-version validation, backup, quarantine, or warning for invalid records structure.
tests_missing: Non-list records fail-closed and preserve exact original bytes.
Mixed invalid entries cannot be silently dropped on the next save.
Explicit migration/backup recovery for older preset-library schemas.
recommended_remediation: Validate schema_version and require records to be a list of valid record objects. On mismatch, return a blocked read/save result and preserve the file; if migration is supported, write a timestamped backup and produce explicit migration evidence before replacement.
remediation_risk: low to medium: stricter loading may expose previously hidden malformed state and needs an operator recovery path
validation_rung: Focused preset-library malformed-state, byte-preservation, migration, atomic-write, and Local API tests using temporary state roots. Real media is not required.
prior_audit_relationship: New current-hash durability defect; no current finding referenced _load_library or preset_library.py.

title: Deployment validation rejects five values accepted by the canonical config contract
observed_behavior: The generated canonical schema and Config model accept LogRetentionDays=0, SourceScanIntervalSeconds=0, ProcessedIndexRefreshSeconds=0, FallbackCpuQuality=null, and OutputSizeMultiplier=null. Invoke-Validation independently requires the first four numeric-loop keys to be greater than zero and casts both null optionals to 0, then rejects them. A direct canonical model probe accepted all five values while equivalent PowerShell casts triggered every setup rejection.
expected_invariant: The deployment validator must accept every value the active canonical contract declares valid, or a documented narrower deployment profile must be encoded as a distinct schema. Optional null and zero-allowed semantics cannot change by entry point.
root_cause: Setup maintains hand-written positive-number and range loops separate from the generated schema, Python numeric policy, and engine schema validation, with PowerShell null-to-zero coercion obscuring optional values.
failure_scenario: An operator opens or validates an otherwise canonical config using zero scan intervals or optional automatic CPU/output sizing. Desktop/schema validation succeeds, but deployment validation reports errors and cannot provide a clean setup handoff; changing values merely to satisfy setup silently changes intended runtime policy.
evidence: Schema lines 1246-1250 and 1710-1720 set minimum=0 for the three zero-allowed integers.
FallbackCpuQuality and OutputSizeMultiplier schemas explicitly allow null.
Config accepted all five values in one direct model probe.
PowerShell [double]$null produced 0 and the exact line predicates rejected both null values and all three zeros.
Engine/Python schema validation also treats scan intervals as minimum zero and the two sizing values as optional.
affected_flows: operator automation using canonical JSON schema
existing_safeguards: Invoke-Validation first runs the shared schema check.
Canonical backend validation and engine schema checks retain their own field bounds.
safeguard_gap: The extra setup checks run after the shared schema and override its valid result without identifying a separate profile or preserving optional-null semantics.
tests_present: Python numeric policy and config contract tests cover many field bounds.
Setup validation performs broad path, dependency, and schema checks.
tests_missing: Table-driven parity test feeding schema-valid boundary/null values through deployment validation.
Generated constraint comparison between setup validation and the canonical schema.
recommended_remediation: Remove duplicate numeric predicates where the shared schema is authoritative, or derive setup checks from the same metadata. Handle optional null before numeric casts and document any intentional deployment-only restriction in a separate explicit contract.
remediation_risk: medium: zero intervals and optional values influence scanning, logging, CPU fallback, and disk estimates, so align semantics without silently changing runtime defaults
validation_rung: Focused canonical Config/schema and setup validation parity tests for boundary/null cases, engine schema/runtime config checks, packaged setup validation, and strict change-packet coverage. Real media is not required.
prior_audit_relationship: New current-hash contract-parity defect; current finding fragments contained no exact setup numeric/null drift finding.
